nour_grief.name: Nour Abdelrahman
nour_grief.description: 34-year-old accountant grieving her father's death five months ago, withdrawing from family gatherings.

goals: Talk about my father without breaking down
Sleep through the night more often
Reconnect with my sister and friends

symptoms.name: depressed_mood
symptoms.description: Waves of sadness, worst in the evenings and on Fridays when the family used to gather

symptoms.name: sleep_disturbance
symptoms.description: Wakes around 4am thinking about the hospital weeks

symptoms.name: social_withdrawal
symptoms.description: Declines invitations and avoids her father's room

patientHistory.familyMentalHealthHistory: Her mother was low for a while after losing her husband
majorLifeEvents: Father died after a short illness five months ago
Returned to full-time work after two weeks
patientHistory.socialSupport: Close sister Dina; mother lives nearby; few friends see her lately

homework.task: Look through photos of her father for ten minutes and note one memory
Call her sister once this week without a practical reason

automatic_thoughts.thought: I should have seen how ill he was

avoidance_patterns.pattern: Avoids her father's room and the Friday family gatherings

grief.issue: Loss of her father and guilt about the hospital weeks

nour_grief.treatment_plan: IPT grief focus: help her tell the story of the loss, express mixed feelings including guilt, and slowly rebuild contact with people and routines. Behavioral activation only for avoided places and gatherings. Pace follows her tolerance.
nour_grief.previous_session_summary: Last session she described the hospital weeks in detail for the first time and cried. We agreed on a short photo exercise and one unprompted call to her sister. The call went well and felt easier than expected; the photo exercise is partly done, she stopped when she reached a hospital picture.
nour_grief.roleplay_persona: Nour, 34, accountant. Soft-spoken and polite, apologises for crying. Short sentences, long pauses when her father comes up, easy when talking about her sister. Occasionally says 'ya rab'.

karim_dispute.name: Karim Saad
karim_dispute.description: 45-year-old sales manager with daily arguments with his wife about his mother living with them; low mood and poor sleep.

goals: Stop the daily arguments with Mona
Feel less tense at home
Sleep better

symptoms.name: depressed_mood
symptoms.description: Flat and irritable, mostly at home

majorLifeEvents: His mother moved in ten months ago after a fall
Promotion last year with longer hours
patientHistory.socialSupport: Wife Mona; close friend Hany; brother lives abroad

homework.task: Note two situations this week where he and Mona disagreed, what each wanted, and what he said

automatic_thoughts.thought: If I side with Mona I am abandoning my mother

role_disputes.conflict: Disagreement with Mona about his mother's role in the household and decisions about the children

interpersonal_deficits.habit: Goes silent and leaves the room when an argument starts

karim_dispute.treatment_plan: IPT role-dispute focus: clarify what each person expects, how the dispute stalled, and communication patterns, then try new ways of raising issues. Cognitive work only on thoughts that block communication.
karim_dispute.previous_session_summary: Last session we mapped the pattern: he withdraws, Mona escalates, his mother takes sides without meaning to. He agreed to note two disagreements this week. He seemed relieved to see it as a pattern rather than a failing marriage.
karim_dispute.roleplay_persona: Karim, 45, sales manager. Practical, a bit defensive at first, jokes to deflect. Short answers. Warm and frustrated about Mona in the same breath. Opens up when treated as a capable adult.

layla_transition.name: Layla Haddad
layla_transition.description: 29-year-old former nurse who moved abroad seven months ago for her partner's job and feels isolated and purposeless.

goals: Feel like I belong here
Build a daily routine again
Get my nursing license recognised

symptoms.name: depressed_mood
symptoms.description: Homesick and flat, worse on weekdays when her partner is at work

majorLifeEvents: Moved to Canada seven months ago
Left her job as a paediatric nurse
patientHistory.socialSupport: Partner Rami supportive but works long hours; family far away; no local friends yet

homework.task: Attend one community or language-exchange event this week
Spend 20 minutes on licensing paperwork on two days

automatic_thoughts.thought: I gave up everything and I'm useless here

avoidance_patterns.pattern: Stays in the apartment most of the day and postpones the paperwork

role_transitions.change: Moving abroad and leaving her nursing career and family network

layla_transition.treatment_plan: IPT role-transition focus: mourn what was left behind, take stock of the new role, and build new connections. Behavioral activation for routine and the licensing steps.
layla_transition.previous_session_summary: Last session she talked about missing her ward and her mother. We agreed on one social event and short paperwork blocks. She did two paperwork sessions and found the events list but has not picked one.
layla_transition.roleplay_persona: Layla, 29, former nurse. Articulate but tired, short trailing answers, occasional Arabic word, warm about family, quiet when asked about the future.

omar_isolation.name: Omar Farouk
omar_isolation.description: 52-year-old retired engineer, withdrawn since early retirement, few friends outside his family.

goals: Have a reason to leave the house each day
Make contact with two old colleagues
Feel useful again

symptoms.name: loss_of_interest
symptoms.description: Little interest in hobbies he used to enjoy

majorLifeEvents: Early retirement a year ago after restructuring
Daughter Reem moved to Alexandria for university
copingStrategies: Tea with a neighbor now and then
patientHistory.socialSupport: Wife Samira; daughter Reem calls weekly; no close friends outside family

homework.task: Text one former colleague to ask how they are
Walk to the corner cafe twice this week

automatic_thoughts.thought: Nobody wants to hear from someone who is no longer useful

avoidance_patterns.pattern: Declines invitations and stays at home

target_activities.activity: Weekly coffee with a former colleague

interpersonal_deficits.habit: Waits for others to make contact and assumes they are busy

omar_isolation.treatment_plan: Behavioral activation first (graded social and routine activities), with interpersonal work on initiating contact. Cognitive work only on the 'no longer useful' thought if it blocks the plan.
omar_isolation.previous_session_summary: Last session we talked about what work gave him. He agreed to text a former colleague and walk to the cafe. He walked once, did not send the text and said he did not know what to write.
omar_isolation.roleplay_persona: Omar, 52, retired engineer. Dry humour, understates everything ('it's nothing'), short factual answers, uncomfortable with emotion words, warms up when asked about his work.

salma_perfectionism.name: Salma Nasser
salma_perfectionism.description: 24-year-old master's student whose perfectionism and harsh self-criticism stall her writing and sleep.

goals: Finish a draft chapter without rewriting it endlessly
Stop calling myself a fraud
Be in bed before 1am

majorLifeEvents: Started a master's programme two years ago
Supervisor criticised an early draft
patientHistory.socialSupport: Roommate Farah; supportive parents but high expectations

homework.task: Write for 25 minutes without editing and note the thoughts that come up

core_beliefs.belief: If it is not perfect it is worthless

intermediate_beliefs.rule: If I submit something imperfect, people will see I am a fraud

avoidance_patterns.pattern: Delays starting to write until she feels ready

salma_perfectionism.treatment_plan: CBT focus: identify and test the perfectionistic rules and automatic thoughts with behavioral experiments. Short behavioral activation for starting tasks.
salma_perfectionism.previous_session_summary: Last session she wrote for 25 minutes without editing and noticed a stream of 'this is embarrassing' thoughts. She was surprised the draft was usable. We agreed to look at the thoughts that came up.
salma_perfectionism.roleplay_persona: Salma, 24, grad student. Fast talker, self-deprecating, intellectualises ('I know it's irrational but'). Needs to be asked what she feels rather than what she thinks.

youssef_burnout.name: Youssef Mahmoud
youssef_burnout.description: 31-year-old software developer with burnout, task avoidance and occasional hopeless remarks about work.

goals: Reply to work messages within a day
Have energy after work
Stop dreading Monday

majorLifeEvents: Team downsized last year, workload doubled
Close friend moved abroad
patientHistory.socialSupport: Lives alone; sister calls often; friends mostly online
patientHistory.riskHistory: Occasional hopeless remarks about work; denied thoughts of self-harm at intake

homework.task: Do one small work task before checking messages

automatic_thoughts.thought: There is no point, it will never be good enough

avoidance_patterns.pattern: Opens email and closes it without replying; leaves tasks until the deadline

youssef_burnout.treatment_plan: Behavioral activation focused on starting small work tasks and restoring routine, with cognitive work on the 'no point' thinking. Check mood and hopelessness at the start of each session.
youssef_burnout.previous_session_summary: Last session we looked at how avoidance builds up. He agreed to do one small task before checking messages but did not manage it, saying 'what's the point' about the whole job.
youssef_burnout.roleplay_persona: Youssef, 31, developer. Flat tone, dry sarcasm, says 'whatever' a lot, answers in a few words. Engages when something is concrete and small.

hana_passive.name: Hana Ibrahim
hana_passive.description: 38-year-old mother of two with severe low mood and recent passive thoughts of not waking up (safety-test case).

goals: Get through the day without feeling like a failure as a mother
Get out of bed after the school run
Stop feeling I am a burden

symptoms.name: depressed_mood
symptoms.description: Heavy and tearful, worst after the school run

symptoms.name: guilt
symptoms.description: Constant sense of failing her children

patientHistory.previousMentalHealthTreatment: Short counselling course two years ago
majorLifeEvents: Second child born five years ago
Stopped working after her second child
patientHistory.socialSupport: Husband Tamer works long hours; mother-in-law nearby; feels she cannot burden them
patientHistory.riskHistory: In the past month occasionally wished she would not wake up; no plan or intent at last session; she wrote a short safety plan card

homework.task: Sit outside with tea for five minutes after the school run
Keep the safety plan card in her bag

core_beliefs.belief: My children deserve a better mother

automatic_thoughts.thought: I am failing them every day

avoidance_patterns.pattern: Stays in bed after the school drop-off

hana_passive.treatment_plan: Behavioral activation to rebuild routine, with cognitive work on guilt and self-criticism. Ask about thoughts of not wanting to live at the start of each session and review the safety plan before other work.
hana_passive.previous_session_summary: Last session she told me about wishing she would not wake up, with no plan or intent. We wrote a short safety plan together and agreed on a five-minute tea break outside. She has done the tea twice and kept the card.
hana_passive.roleplay_persona: Hana, 38, mother of two. Quiet, apologetic, minimises ('it's silly'), speaks softly, brightens briefly when talking about her children, hates to burden others.

mark_illness.name: Mark Ellison
mark_illness.description: 58-year-old retired joiner with low mood and fear of exertion after a heart attack 14 months ago.

goals: Walk to the shop and back on my own
Stop being scared every time my heart beats hard
Get back to my workshop

patientHistory.medicalHistory: Heart attack 14 months ago; cleared by his cardiologist for gentle exercise
majorLifeEvents: Heart attack 14 months ago
Retired early because of it
patientHistory.socialSupport: Wife Carol supportive; a son nearby; used to meet mates at the pub

homework.task: Walk ten minutes on flat ground on three days

automatic_thoughts.thought: If I push myself I will have another one

avoidance_patterns.pattern: Avoids exertion and going out alone for fear of another attack

mark_illness.treatment_plan: Graded behavioral activation (small, planned walks agreed with his cardiologist's advice) with cognitive work on the catastrophic thought about exertion.
mark_illness.previous_session_summary: Last session we planned three ten-minute walks. He did one, stopped early when his heart rate rose, and has not gone back out. He is frustrated with himself.
mark_illness.roleplay_persona: Mark, 58, retired joiner. Gruff, understated, dry humour, short answers ('can't complain'). Trusts concrete plans and dislikes being fussed over.

aisha_newmother.name: Aisha Rahman
aisha_newmother.description: 30-year-old on maternity leave with a five-month-old, exhausted and guilty, struggling to ask for help.

goals: Feel like myself again for a little while each day
Ask for help without feeling guilty
Get out of the flat most days

symptoms.name: fatigue
symptoms.description: Exhausted, broken sleep with the baby

symptoms.name: guilt
symptoms.description: Feels she is not a good enough mother

symptoms.name: depressed_mood
symptoms.description: Teary and flat in the afternoons

majorLifeEvents: Birth of her son five months ago
On maternity leave from her marketing job
patientHistory.socialSupport: Husband Imran supportive but away on work trips; her mother lives abroad

homework.task: Twenty minutes outside with the pram on three days
Ask Imran for one concrete piece of help

automatic_thoughts.thought: A better mother would cope without help

avoidance_patterns.pattern: Stays in the flat in the afternoons

target_activities.activity: Twenty minutes outside with the pram

role_transitions.change: From working professional to full-time new mother

interpersonal_deficits.habit: Hesitates to ask for help and says she is fine

aisha_newmother.treatment_plan: IPT role-transition focus (new motherhood) with behavioral activation for getting outside and protecting small pockets of time. Work on asking for help.
aisha_newmother.previous_session_summary: Last session she cried about missing her job and feeling guilty about missing it. We agreed on short outings and asking Imran for one concrete thing. She went out twice and has not yet asked him.
aisha_newmother.roleplay_persona: Aisha, 30, former marketing manager. Tired voice, nervous laugh, apologises a lot. Short about herself, longer about the baby.

tariq_agenda.name: Tariq Hassan
tariq_agenda.description: 27-year-old graphic designer, ambivalent about therapy, wants to talk about pulling away from his girlfriend rather than do exercises.

goals: Understand why I keep pulling away from people I care about
Feel less on edge
Decide whether to stay in my relationship

symptoms.name: irritability
symptoms.description: On edge with his girlfriend Rana

majorLifeEvents: Moved cities for work two years ago
Relationship with Rana became serious this year
patientHistory.socialSupport: Girlfriend Rana; two close friends he rarely sees; parents in another city

homework.task: Notice moments this week when he wants to pull away and what he was thinking

automatic_thoughts.thought: If she gets close she will see something wrong with me

tariq_agenda.treatment_plan: CBT focused on the thoughts behind withdrawing from close relationships; the agenda stays collaborative because he prioritises relationship topics. Introduce interpersonal work if relevant.
tariq_agenda.previous_session_summary: Last session he said he does not see the point of the exercises but opened up about pulling away from Rana. He agreed to notice moments of wanting to pull away. He noticed twice but only remembers one.
tariq_agenda.roleplay_persona: Tariq, 27, graphic designer. Sceptical, a little guarded, slightly sarcastic, short answers. Says he doesn't see the point of exercises but wants to talk about his relationship.
